text:
Denver Barkey was the 95th pick in 2023, a 5'10" centre out of the London Knights, and he's turned into one of the Flyers' most reliable young players. Broad Street Hockey called him an analytical darling this month, and it's easy to see why: Philadelphia takes 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five, far better than without him on a team that is getting badly out-chanced overall.

He has eight points in 17 games, half of them on the power play, and he opened the scoring in Calgary on Nov. 8 by burying a rebound. He's a passer who rarely shoots (9th percentile shot strength by NHL Edge), so his value shows up in his linemates' chances and in the ones he takes away: Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting noticeably fewer chances with him out there last season (91st percentile). Nothing in his scoring looks lucky. At 21 and about 14.5 minutes a night, the question is how long the Flyers keep him in a depth role. Our projection is around 37 points.
